Series::sum_to_size¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series Series::sum_to_size(pluss::msharp::RangeView::Int size) const

Reversing A Broadcast By Summation¶

sum_to_size() reduces a Series to a shape from which it could have been broadcast to the receiver’s shape. It exists primarily for shape-correct reverse rules: if a smaller operand was repeated implicitly across an operation, its sensitivity must sum the repeated contributions rather than retain the expanded shape.

Dimensions are aligned from the right. A target dimension is valid when it is equal to the corresponding receiver extent or is 1; a leading receiver dimension may also be removed. Every removed dimension and every dimension contracted to one is summed. Unlike a general sum(), the retained axes and their singleton extents are inferred from the target shape itself.

For receiver shape [2,3,4]:

  • {1,3,1} sums axes zero and two and keeps both singleton axes;

  • {3,4} sums only the leading axis;

  • {} sums every lane to a rank-zero scalar;

  • {2,3,4} requests no reduction.

size cannot have more dimensions than the receiver, and an aligned target extent other than 1 must equal the receiver extent. Negative extents are not valid shapes. The result retains the receiver’s dtype and platform.

Ownership And Reverse Mode¶

The operation is out of place. A genuine reduction allocates a result; the equal-shape case returns an equivalent Series without changing the receiver. In reverse mode, output sensitivity is broadcast back across every reduced axis, exactly reversing the forward sum-to-shape relation.

Examples¶

1. Contract broadcast axes while retaining rank¶

const auto cube = pluss::series::arange(
    1.0, 25.0, 1.0, pluss::ScalarType::Float64).reshape({2, 3, 4});
pluss::series::print(std::cout, cube.sum_to_size({1, 3, 1}));

Output¶

Series(shape=[1,3,1], strides=[3,1,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data[0, :, :] =
⎡  68.0000 ⎤
⎢ 100.0000 ⎥
⎣ 132.0000 ⎦

For each middle-axis position, all two leading lanes and all four trailing lanes contribute to one sum.

2. Reduce to a scalar shape¶

pluss::series::print(std::cout, cube.sum_to_size({}));

Output¶

Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=300.0000

An empty target shape means rank zero, not an empty Series.

3. Request the existing shape¶

pluss::series::print(std::cout, cube.sum_to_size({2, 3, 4}));

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3,4], strides=[12,4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=24, contiguous=true)
data[0, :, :] =
⎡ 1.0000  2.0000  3.0000  4.0000 ⎤
⎢ 5.0000  6.0000  7.0000  8.0000 ⎥
⎣ 9.0000 10.0000 11.0000 12.0000 ⎦

data[1, :, :] =
⎡ 13.0000 14.0000 15.0000 16.0000 ⎤
⎢ 17.0000 18.0000 19.0000 20.0000 ⎥
⎣ 21.0000 22.0000 23.0000 24.0000 ⎦

No axis is summed when every extent already agrees.

4. Broadcast sensitivity back to the receiver¶

auto tracked = cube.clone();
tracked.tracks_slope_(true);
tracked.sum_to_size({1, 3, 1}).sum().reverse();
pluss::series::print(std::cout, tracked.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,3,4], strides=[12,4,1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=24, contiguous=true)
data[0, :, :] =
⎡ 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 ⎤
⎢ 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 ⎥
⎣ 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 ⎦

data[1, :, :] =
⎡ 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 ⎤
⎢ 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 ⎥
⎣ 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 1.0000 ⎦

5. Reject a shape that could not broadcast to the receiver¶

try {
  (void)cube.sum_to_size({2, 2, 4});
} catch (const std::exception& error) {
  std::cout << error.what() << '\n';
}

Output¶

sum_to_size: incompatible target dimension

The middle extent 2 is neither the receiver extent 3 nor singleton 1.

See Also¶

  • sum() performs caller-selected reductions.

  • broadcast_to() performs the opposite shape expansion.

  • reshape() changes shape without reducing values.
